acceptance_checks: On Windows, recursive linting of target `src/` with `ignore-paths = ["^src/gen/.*$"]` excludes files under `src\gen\` while continuing to lint non-matching files such as `src\region_selection.py`.
A mixed path such as `src/\gen\about.py` matches a Posix-anchored pattern such as `^src/gen/.*$`.
The same mixed path matches an equivalent Windows-separator pattern.
A pattern written specifically for the original raw mixed-separator string continues to match that raw candidate.
Relative paths remain relative and absolute paths remain absolute during matching.
Direct file inputs, recursive discovery roots and files, package submodules, and namespace submodules use the same canonical `ignore-paths` comparison behavior.
Existing `ignore` and `ignore-patterns` basename tests remain unchanged and pass.
Add regression coverage for mixed-separator paths to the ignore-path normalization/matching unit tests.
Add an end-to-end or lint-level regression test covering the reported anchored pattern with recursive target spelling `src/` under Windows-style path construction.
Run the targeted configuration and recursive-lint test suites successfully.
confirmed_decisions: Apply the fix centrally to all full-path `ignore-paths` comparisons, not only recursively discovered paths.
Normalize separators only; do not resolve, absolutize, relativize, or otherwise rewrite paths.
Limit the behavior change to `ignore-paths`; retain existing basename behavior for `ignore` and `ignore-patterns`.
Evaluate each `ignore-paths` regex against both fully Posix and fully Windows separator forms.
Also evaluate against the original raw path string for backward compatibility with patterns that intentionally match an existing mixed-separator representation.
Preserve existing regex `match` behavior and configured-pattern parsing semantics.
summary: Fix `ignore-paths` so every full-path comparison is robust to mixed separators. For each path evaluated by `ignore-paths`, preserve its relative or absolute form and evaluate the configured regex against three candidates: the original raw string, a fully Posix-separator form, and a fully Windows-separator form. Apply this centrally to all `ignore-paths` comparisons, including recursive discovery, direct inputs, packages, and namespace-module expansion. Do not change basename extraction or the behavior of `ignore` and `ignore-patterns`. Existing regex matching semantics remain unchanged.
